univ_stance.quote: Generative AI tools are considered online learning support platforms and may not be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by an instructor
univ_stance.note: Instructors may allow or prohibit, but the stated default under the Student Conduct Code is no use without explicit authorization, so the default is coded (codebook: code the default).

univ_tone.quote: Active engagement with course materials, critical thinking and judgment, and expression of original ideas should never be outsourced to technology.
univ_tone.note: The page is mostly procedure, but its required statements are framed around scholastic dishonesty, copyright, and data security, and it ends on this warning.

dept_stance.quote: CS&E faculty encourage students to utilize AI throughout their educational journey from introductory courses to senior seminars.
dept_stance.note: Only department text on AI found; the department's academic conduct policy does not mention AI. The same paragraph says some introductory courses ban AI and many others allow it with conditions.

dept_tone.quote: AI is a powerful tool that can improve your productivity as long as you have the fundamental knowledge to understand its limitations and use it effectively.

collaboration.quote: The emphasis is on experimentation, problem-solving, and understanding personal strengths and growth areas when collaborating with AI tools.
collaboration.note: One sentence, describing the CSCI 2521 course; no page reviewed develops AI as a partner further.

disclosure.quote: Indicate how students will acknowledge GenAI use, including citation practices and required documentation
disclosure.note: Borderline: the requirement is addressed to instructors of courses that allow AI, telling them to set how students acknowledge it, rather than stated directly to students.

se_courses.note: CSCI 5801 Software Engineering I has no public syllabus; CSCI 5802 Software Engineering II (spring 2024 page, the newest reachable) has an academic integrity section that does not mention AI. CSCI 4821 GenAI for Software Engineering (new in fall 2026) is described only in news, with no public syllabus.

univ_stance.quote: It is important for faculty to clearly outline the expectations of generative AI usage at the beginning of a course to avoid frustration in students’ learning processes.
univ_stance.note: No university-wide default found; the teaching guidance leaves the rule to each course and its division.

univ_tone.quote: there is an abundance of ethical considerations that demand careful attention.
univ_tone.note: The guidelines page is mostly FERPA, HIPAA, ownership, bias and privacy risks. The parent overview page (curl blocked, read in the browser) is more upbeat about benefits; the page with the rules was coded.

disclosure.quote: Transparency: Respect intellectual property rights by acknowledging the sources of AI-generated content used in your work.
disclosure.cue_reason: Listed under example guidelines that faculty can share with students, so it is advice for courses to adopt, not a rule; that makes it encouraged even though the sentence is an imperative.

se_courses.note: The only page for EN.601.421 on jhu.edu is from Fall 2018, before ChatGPT; codebook v1 codes it 'not addressed'. Flagged for codebook v2: course pages from before 2023 should not count. The Spring 2024 syllabus on Notion did not load.

univ_stance.quote: Include a statement that clearly defines the acceptable use of AI for your course.
univ_stance.cue_reason: The sentence is a required element of every Valpo syllabus, addressed to the instructor, so each course sets its own rule; no university default is stated.
univ_stance.note: Required syllabus elements (revised 2025), not a stand-alone policy page; the Honor Council page also tells faculty to address AI in their syllabi.

univ_tone.quote: Do not mindlessly use AI tools in place of your own thinking, analysis, and general learning
univ_tone.note: The suggested AI language is a list of warnings (do not, mistakes, verify); the Honor Council and CITAL pages focus on misuse cases and detection.

disclosure.quote: If you use AI, always provide evidence of how AI tool contributed to your work.
disclosure.cue_reason: Part of the suggested syllabus language that instructors may adopt, not a rule on its own; saying how AI contributed is a disclosure.

se_courses.note: CS 358 Software Design and Development: the only syllabus found (Spring 2010) now returns HTTP 403.
